 Live .  12,765 viewing 12765 viewing England openers move beyond 100-0 against Sri Lanka
 Thu 29 Oct 2026 , Men's One Day International Series Sri Lanka vs England (batting), in play Sri Lanka Sri Lanka In Play England England Yet to bat 140 -0 ( 19.5 ) England are 140 for 0 with 30.1 overs remaining Sri Lanka: yet to bat England innings: 140 for 0 from 19.5 overs, in play
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 Openers Banton & Duckett share century stand 
 Sri Lanka win toss and bowl first in Lahore
 England already eliminated from tri-series
 South Africa v Australia live text 
 Close form Have your say on England men this winter
 Get involved Live Reporting
 by Ffion Wynne
 Post published at 09:26 GMT 09:26 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Sri Lanka need to find a way of applying some pressure to England. 
 Everything is pretty straightforward.
 It is all too easy for England out in the middle.
 7 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 132-0 published at 19 overs 19 overs 
 Ben Duckett is all over Sri Lanka here. He is able to adjust to every plan they are trying.
 This time, Janith Liyanage tries a couple of short balls but Duckett dispatches them both for four. 
 21 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Inglis out after reaching second Test century published at 09:23 GMT 09:23 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Australia have lost their first wicket on day three of the third Test, but not before Josh Inglis reached his second Test century.
 The right-hander got there in 132 balls before edging Simon Harmer behind for 102.
 He still has Australia in a position of strength. They are 377-5, leading by 48 on first innings.
 Follow the latest here. 
 10 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 122-0 published at 18 overs 18 overs 
 As Alex says, Tom Banton's done brilliantly well but in such good batting conditions, he would be desperate to turn this one into three figures knowing that Jacob Bethell is waiting in the wings.
 Image source, Cricviz 
 19 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:21 GMT 09:21 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 Tom Banton has got a good average at the top of the order, 45. 
 He has had a good tournament, but then he has not been able to capitalise on the 50s or the starts that he has got. 
 12 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 50 for Tom Banton published at 17.1 overs 17.1 overs 
 Eng 117-0 
 Image source, Reuters Tom Banton reaches another half-century - his fifth in his past six ODI innings. 
 An exceptional return to the format for England's newest opener. 
 60 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:19 GMT 09:19 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 England will be desperate for Joe Root to get in and score some runs before he gets off to Australia. 
 He has been shy of runs in this tournament so far. He is crucial to England's success. 
 24 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 116-0 published at 17 overs 17 overs 
 Here's the all-rounder Janith Liyanage, who struggled with the ball in England's 429 (he wasn't alone there, in fairness) but was the hero with the bat. 
 He starts well here though, as Banton and Duckett get themselves resettled after drinks by ticking five runs off the over.
 8 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:16 GMT 09:16 GMT 
 England have upped their run-rate in recent overs.
 Image source, Cricviz 
 15 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 09:14 GMT 09:14 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' at the top of this page to have your say 
 England will probably win this game comfortably because there’s zero pressure on it. Until they get in a coach who can instil some mental toughness in the players we will continue to crumble under pressure and win nothing meaningful.
 Ollie, Thirsk 
 126 68 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:12 GMT 09:12 GMT 
 Alex Hartley 
Former England bowler on Test Match Special 
 A strange feeling about today. 
 End of school vibes where your teacher just puts on a movie and says, 'That's our lesson today'. 
 The way England are going, they are on for another mammoth score. 
 49 12 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 drinks break Eng 111-0 published at 16 overs 16 overs 
 Duckett 61, Banton 47 
 Eeek. 
 Ben Duckett makes it three boundaries in the over, pulling firmly again before drilling another through the off side. 
 Problems for Sri Lanka, and they now have a timely drinks' break to reassess their plans.
 30 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 50 for Ben Duckett published at 15.1 overs 15.1 overs 
 Eng 103-0 
 Image source, Getty Images Ben Duckett pulls into the leg side to bring up his fifty and the hundred partnership with the same shot. 
 It's a belting pitch, and he's just picked up where he left off from his century a few days ago. 
 62 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 99-0 published at 15 overs 15 overs 
 Yep, he's on the charge now.
 Banton skips down the pitch and launches Arachchige over mid-wicket for the first six of the day. 
 68 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:04 GMT 09:04 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 I hope these two keep playing with the intent that they are against the spin here. 
 Keep the scoreboard going. England still have Joe Root and Harry Brook to come, then down into the powerful middle order.
 They have an opportunity here to post another mammoth total. It is all in England's hands. 
 37 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 89-0 published at 14.1 overs 14.1 overs 
 Image source, Reuters On cue! 
 Tom Banton slams this one straight down the ground, over the head of mid-off for four. 
 25 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 85-0 published at 14 overs 14 overs 
 Duckett 47, Banton 35 
 We're whizzing through the overs of spin now.
 There are cries of "catch!" from fielders as Tom Banton lofts one aerially towards long-off, but his lack of timing ensures that it lands safely. Still no real sign of aggression towards the spinners yet, so it'll be interesting to see if and when one of them flicks the switch. 
 9 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:00 GMT 09:00 GMT 
 Steven Finn 
Former England fast bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 It will be interesting to see if England will be stubborn and truly believe that having those all-rounders in the middle making up the fifth bowler is going to work for them moving towards that World Cup. 
 I think Sam Curran has come off a long lay off from injury, and to be thrust into a series like this was always going to be challenging. But it is good that England want to give them opportunities and that they don't turf someone after one game.
 18 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eng 81-0 published at 13 overs 13 overs 
 Image source, Reuters Spin from both ends - here's Sahan Arachchige. 
 Banton and Duckett are cautious against his first over, just ticking the singles from it, but they're still setting up for a big total here. 
 12 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 08:56 GMT 08:56 GMT 
 England’s opening pair are averaging 58.83 in 2026 - only India (77.83) are averaging more.
England's openers have also passed fifty on six occasions this year - no side has passed the milsetone more often.
